profile.profile: No sources support the existence of a dance named Pique. the sources only document Juanita Emylyn Pique, known professionally as Mitzi Mayfair, an American dancer and stage and film actress born in 1914. Archival French-language texts reference the word 'pique-nique' in community notices, but no traditional dance by this name is described. Consequently, technical dance profiles cannot be derived from the available documentation.
profile.profile_long: No sources support the existence of a dance named Pique. The historical record available in the sources focuses exclusively on Juanita Emylyn Pique, an American dancer, stage, and film actress who performed under the stage name Mitzi Mayfair. Born in Fulton, Kentucky on June 6, 1914, she grew up in St. Louis, Missouri and began performing professionally in vaudeville and stage productions during the 1930s. Her career included appearances in Broadway productions such as Flo Ziegfeld's Follies in 1931 and Harry Akst's Calling All Stars in 1934, as well as film work in Vitaphone musical shorts and Four Jills in a Jeep. Other references in digitized historical newspapers use the term 'pique-nique' in the context of community gatherings and picnics in Manitoba, but do not describe a dance form. Because no sources describe choreography, music, or technique for a dance named Pique, all technical parameters remain undescribed.
